;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]]
**[[2019–20 Western Libya campaign]]
***Eight [[mass grave]]s containing hundreds of bodies are discovered in western [[Libya]], most of them in the town of [[Tarhuna]]. The [[Government of National Accord]] (GNA) says the remains are of captured GNA fighters and civilians, apparent evidence of [[war crime]]s. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/expresses-horror-reported-mass-graves-discovery-libya-200611201231621.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[June 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
**Four people are killed and eight others injured by the [[improvised explosive device|bombing]] of a [[mosque]] in [[Kabul]]. No group claimed responsibility. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attack/four-killed-and-many-injured-in-blast-in-kabul-mosque-ministry-of-interior-idUSKBN23J1DH (Reuters)]
*About 30 [[Indian people|Indians]] cross [[India–Nepal border|the border]] into [[Nepal]] and clash with [[Nepal Police|Nepali police]] when stopped in the district of [[Sarlahi]]. Nepali [[border guard]]s opened fire, killing one man and injuring two. According to police, the forces fired when one of the men snatched a gun from them. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/firing-nepal-india-border-leaves-dead-strained-ties-200612104607012.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Business and economy
*[[Sanrio]] founder and CEO [[Shintaro Tsuji]], whose company is best known for creating [[Hello Kitty]], announces he will resign on July 1 citing a need to "transform the company to better respond to today's rapidly changing business environment." His grandson Tomokuni Tsuji is expected to replace him. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-53029110 (BBC News)]
*[[Brazil]]'s [[government of Brazil|state]]-run oil company [[Petrobras]] says it will not do business with [[Oil tanker|tankers]] that visited [[Venezuela]] in the past year, adhering to [[International sanctions during the Venezuelan crisis|sanctions]] placed by the [[United States]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-brazil-sanctions-tankers/brazils-petrobras-says-it-will-not-hire-oil-tankers-that-visited-venezuela-idUSKBN23K019?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[LGBTQ rights in the United States]], [[Abortion in the United States]]
**The [[United States Department of Health and Human Services|U.S. Department of Health and Human Services]] removes protections against discrimination within [[Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act|Obamacare]] for [[Transgender|transgender people]] and women seeking [[abortion]]s. The move is condemned by civil rights groups and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] officials. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-healthcare-transgender/u-s-health-agency-reverses-obamacare-transgender-protections-idUSKBN23J37M?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Slavery in Australia]]
**[[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] apologizes for saying there was "no [[slavery]]" in [[Australia]]. He says that he was referring specifically to the fact that the first Australian colony of [[New South Wales]] was set up without the widespread use of [[slave labor]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/06/12/australia/australia-slavery-scott-morrison-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Lebanese liquidity crisis]]
**Hundreds protest over the handling of the country's economic crisis, many calling for [[Hassan Diab]]'s [[government of Lebanon|government]] to resign. The [[Lebanese pound]] has lost 70 percent of its value since October, when protests began. The government announced the central bank will begin injecting more [[United States dollar]]s into the market on Monday. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-53031683 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/ajimpact/protests-rock-lebanon-currency-collapses-200612060707797.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2020 Republican Party presidential primaries]], [[Donald Trump 2020 presidential campaign]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces the [[Make America Great Again|MAGA Rally]] that was to be held on June 19, in [[Tulsa, Oklahoma]], is rescheduled to June 20. The rally's original date had been widely criticized because the 19th is [[Juneteenth]], the date commemorating the end of American slavery. The location was also criticized due to it being where the 1921 [[Tulsa race massacre]] took place, because of the ongoing [[George Floyd protests]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/12/politics/donald-trump-tulsa-rally-juneteenth/index.html (CNN)] [https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/502573-trump-reschedules-tulsa-rally-after-criticism-of-overlap-with-juneteenth (''The Hill'')]
*[[President of Burundi|President-elect of Burundi]] [[Évariste Ndayishimiye]] is set to take power immediately, days after the death of incumbent [[Pierre Nkurunziza]], as the [[Constitutional Court of Burundi|constitutional court]] says "it is not necessary to have an interim period", and that Ndayishimiye should be sworn-in "as soon as possible". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-burundi-politics/burundis-president-elect-to-take-power-immediately-after-death-of-former-leader-idUSKBN23J27O?il=0 (Reuters)]
*On the 122nd anniversary of the [[Philippines]]'s [[Philippine Declaration of Independence|independence from Spain]], more than a thousand protestors march at the main campus of the [[University of the Philippines Diliman|University of the Philippines]] in [[Metro Manila|Manila]] to protest a controversial anti-terrorism bill introduced by [[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-philippines-rights-protests/philippine-protesters-rally-over-controversial-anti-terror-bill-idUSKBN23J1FG?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Science and technology
*[[Twitter]] says it has [[Twitter suspensions|removed]] a network of more than 170,000 accounts it says were spreading pro-[[Communist Party of China]] [[propaganda]] on the [[social media]] platform, saying the Chinese-based network had links to earlier [[government of China|state]]-backed operations on [[Facebook]] and [[YouTube]]. More than a thousand [[Russia]]-based misinformation accounts are also removed. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-53018455 (BBC News)]
